question: If 3 cos² θ + 1 = 4 sin θ, 0° θ θ is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Test standard angles for **0° [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 3 cos² θ + 1 = 4 sin θ

**Formula Used:** cos² θ = 1 − sin² θ; sec² θ = 1 / cos² θ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b7d5e6c294f1bfeb6ff1cafc91dd0cfecf54b4a6276b3db266b3673055225cac.png] 

⇒ 3(1 − sin² θ) + 1 = 4 sin θ

⇒ 3 − 3 sin² θ + 1 = 4 sin θ

⇒ 3 sin² θ + 4 sin θ − 4 = 0

⇒ 3 sin² θ + 6 sin θ − 2 sin θ − 4 = 0

⇒ 3 sin θ(sin θ + 2) − 2(sin θ + 2) = 0

⇒ (3 sin θ − 2)(sin θ + 2) = 0

⇒ **sin θ = 2/3** (Since sin θ cannot be −2)

⇒ cos² θ = 1 − (2/3)² = 1 − 4/9 = 5/9

⇒ sec² θ = 1 / (5/9) = 9/5

**∴ The correct answer is 9/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities include sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ, and 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ.

Reciprocal Relations

sec θ = 1/cos θ, cosec θ = 1/sin θ, and cot θ = 1/tan θ.

Pythagorean Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base².</p
